governing_document.reason: 2025-18469 is the final rule (Amendment 39-23153, AD 2025-19-13). The thread has no correction document, so the final rule's regulatory text controls. The proposed rule 2025-10764 does not control.

eligible_parts.description: An HPT 1st-stage hub or HPT 2nd-stage hub whose P/N and S/N combination is not listed in table 1 to paragraph (g). The definition names no part numbers of its own.

required_actions.description: For engines with an installed part whose P/N and S/N are identified in table 1 to paragraph (g): remove the affected part from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation. This is due at the next engine shop visit after the effective date, before exceeding the applicable removal cycle limit in table 1, or within 100 flight cycles from the effective date, whichever occurs later.

installation_prohibitions.description: After the effective date of the AD, do not install in any engine an HPT 1st-stage hub or HPT 2nd-stage hub that has a P/N and S/N listed in table 1 to paragraph (g).

ambiguities.description: The compliance time names three elements: the next engine shop visit after the effective date, before exceeding the table 1 removal cycle limit, and within 100 flight cycles from the effective date. These are joined by a single 'whichever occurs later', with no punctuation showing which elements are being compared. This decides whether removal is forced without a shop visit and what the latest permissible removal point is.
readings: Reading 1: The deadline is the later of (a) reaching the part's table 1 removal cycle limit (cycles since new) and (b) 100 flight cycles after the effective date. The part must be removed at the next engine shop visit after the effective date, or by that deadline if no shop visit happens first.

Reading 2: 'Whichever occurs later' compares 'at the next engine shop visit after the effective date, before exceeding the removal cycle limit' with 'within 100 flight cycles from the effective date'. Removal is due at the later of those two points.
Reading 3: Removal is required only at the next engine shop visit after the effective date. The cycle limit / 100 flight cycle clause only qualifies how late that shop visit may occur.

ambiguities.description: The engine shop visit definition refers to 'separation of any major mating engine flanges, H-P'. This decides whether a given maintenance event is a shop visit, and so when paragraph (g) comes due.
readings: Reading 1: 'H-P' means the range of major mating flanges from H through P inclusive.
Reading 2: 'H-P' names only the two flanges H and P, or a single flange designated H-P.

notes: No correction document is in the thread. The final rule's regulatory text matches the NPRM (2025-10764), except that paragraph (a) changed from Comments Due Date to Effective Date. The preamble states the AD was adopted as proposed except for minor editorial changes.

The applicability paragraph (c) covers all listed engine models with no part condition. Paragraph (g) applies only to engines with an installed part whose P/N and S/N combination appears in table 1. Screening must match both P/N and S/N, not P/N alone.

The installation prohibition in paragraph (h) applies to all engines within the applicability. The preamble response to comments confirms the applicability was deliberately kept to all listed models so that this prohibition reaches every engine.

HPT 1st-stage hub S/N PKLBSK9287 has a removal cycle limit of only 100 cycles since new. The 100 flight cycles after the effective date limit in paragraph (g) may control for it, depending on how the compliance time is read.
The table 1 title reads 'Affected HPT 1st Stage and HPT 2nd Stage Hubs'. The row component names are written 'HPT 1st-stage hub' and 'HPT 2nd-stage hub', and those are the names recorded here.
The preamble estimates two U.S.-registered engines are affected, both needing HPT 1st-stage hub replacement and none needing HPT 2nd-stage hub replacement.
No material is incorporated by reference (paragraph (l)). Paragraph (b) lists no affected ADs.
